transcript:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a KV-cache-only quantization bakeoff (FP8 vs INT8 vs AWQ-GPTQ variants) against redwood-3b-open to measure memory and tail latency impact. posting summary + logs

kevin: awesome, can you paste the config and key numbers? :eyes:

maria: config: 
```
model: redwood-3b-open
seq_len: 2048
batch: 1
kv_only_quant: true
variants: [fp8-kv, int8-kv, awq-kv]
metric: perplexity + p99 latency
hw: gpus=v100x4 (dedicated), cpu=32
```

maria: high-level numbers (baseline fp16 full model): mem=12.4 GB working set, p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=140ms, ppl=6.92

sophia: nice. results?

maria: results (single-shot generation workload):
```
fp8-kv:  mem=9.1 GB (-26.6%), p50=17ms, p95=58ms, p99=130ms, ppl=6.95 (+0.4% delta)
int8-kv: mem=7.8 GB (-37.1%), p50=16ms, p95=54ms, p99=118ms, ppl=7.12 (+2.9% delta)
awq-kv: mem=7.6 GB (-38.7%), p50=16ms, p95=55ms, p99=125ms, ppl=6.98 (+0.9% delta)
```

kevin: so int8-kv is best for memory and latency but has the largest ppl regression. AWQ looks like a good compromise.

dylan: do we have headroom at different sequence lengths? e.g., seq=4096 will amplify kv memory impact.

maria: ran seq=4096 quick run (same batch):
```
baseline fp16 mem=22.0 GB
fp8-kv mem=16.2 GB
int8-kv mem=14.0 GB
p99 latency deltas: +25% (fp8), +18% (int8) vs baseline at 4096
```

sophia: interesting that p99 improves for int8 at 2048 but degrades relative at 4096. could be batching/serialization overheads.

maria: suspected: kernel scheduling + alignment inefficiencies for larger KV pages in fp8 path. instrumented traces shows more CPU->GPU memcpy for fp8 rollout at long seq.

kevin: can you paste the trace snippet? small sample is fine.

maria: trace (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:09Z] kv_pack: memcpy 1.4GB -> GPU (32ms)
[2026-03-17T10:12:09Z] fp8_dequantize_kernel launch (grid=128) (kernel_ms=6)
[2026-03-17T10:12:09Z] attention_kernel launch (grid=1024) (kernel_ms=28)
[2026-03-17T10:12:09Z] kv_unpack: memcpy 1.4GB <- GPU (30ms)
```

maria: for int8 path memcpy sizes smaller due to denser packing -> less CPU/GPU transfer time overall.

dylan: what about quality checks other than ppl? any rouge/qa EM on eval sets?

maria: ran two evals: prompt-completion pass@1 on short QA and code generation success rate on unit tests.
```
QA EM (devset 2k): baseline=78.1, fp8-kv=77.6 (-0.5), int8-kv=75.2 (-2.9), awq-kv=77.9 (-0.2)
Code unit tests (suite 200): baseline=92.5%, fp8-kv=92.0%, int8-kv=89.0%, awq-kv=91.8%
```

sophia: ok int8 impact is nontrivial for correctness-sensitive flows.

kevin: any configs to mitigate int8 quality hit? mixed-precision for some layers? per-layer KV fallback?

maria: tried hybrid: int8-kv + keep keys for first 2 transformer layers in fp16 (hybrid-kv). results:
```
hybrid-kv mem=8.9GB, p99=122ms, QA EM=77.2 (-0.9 vs baseline)
```

maria: so hybrid recovers most quality while keeping mem benefits ~28% reduction.

ci-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/kv-quant/1783456789/artifacts.tar.gz

sophia: nice. recommend run: expand hybrid sweep across 3-5 models and check long-tail prompts.

dylan: also want to try prioritized KV cache eviction + smaller kv-page packing for fp8 to reduce memcpy spikes.

kevin: deployment recommendation draft?

maria: my suggestion:
- latency-sensitive prod (low-regression tolerance): use hybrid-kv (int8 with top-2-layers fp16) — good latency/mem tradeoff and quality ~<1% delta
- throughput cost-optimizing batchy workloads: int8-kv (full) for internal-only, low-correction pipelines where small quality regressions tolerated
- highest-quality routes: fp8-kv or fp16 for customer-facing completions with strict correctness

maria: next steps: schedule sweep across redwood-7b-open and redwood-1.4b, add per-layer sensitivity plotting, and run longer seq tails (8k) to validate memcpy mitigation ideas.

kevin: +1. please open task in eng-ml board and mark priority high for KPI-sensitive customers.

sophia: thanks for the run, super actionable :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

maria: thanks all — putting full logs and eval artifacts in the ticket.
